name: Graphene acid-recovery membrane
subtitle: recovers acid from battery recycling for reuse

effects.effect: graphene lets protons through but stops every atom and molecule

effect: graphene lets protons through but stops every atom and molecule
how: Recycling lithium batteries means dissolving them in strong acid, and the spent acid, thick with metals, is costly to neutralise and dump. A graphene sheet lets the acid's hydrogen ions through while stopping every dissolved metal, so the acid is pulled out clean for reuse and the metals are left behind concentrated.
obstacle: Graphene sheets big enough for a plant still crack and leak, and they need supports that survive strong acid.
why: Proton sieving works in micron-scale lab devices; never applied to recycling.
real: Graphene-oxide membranes have been studied as proton-permselective membranes for recovering acid from metal-laden waste (J. Membrane Sci. 2021), but no demonstration on battery-recycling leachate with pristine graphene proton transport was found.
